summary: Orphaned service token rotations triggering multi-account lockouts and anomalous auth activity
description:
Issue summary: Multiple user accounts across two regions entered a brief lockout state and we observed a surge of failed token exchange attempts tied to a set of legacy service tokens that were scheduled for rotation. Impact: Intermittent login failures for ~12 engineers and two service accounts; alert storm to PagerDuty; potential phishing correlation under investigation. Environment: Production (auth/identity plane) in us-east primary, failover in eu-west.

Observed behavior: Around 2026-03-10T06:57Z automated token rotation job for legacy-service-tokens triggered several concurrent refresh requests to the OAuth token-exchange endpoint. A subset of orphaned tokens (previously issued to decommissioned CI runners and not fully removed from the token store) started cycling, leading to repeated refresh attempts that generated account lockout conditions for user identities associated with those tokens. Concurrently, we saw an increase in suspicious external consent grant requests to an old AD app registered in the tenant. Hypothesis: A prior phishing incident exposed or orphaned refresh tokens; automated rotation job re-used the stale entries and amplified the auth failures.

Impact details: Authentication failures surfaced as 401/403s for interactive logins and 429/lockout events for some SSO flows. No customer data exfiltration confirmed at time of triage. This is an internal incident (privileged/internal accounts affected).
timeline: 2026-03-10T06:45Z - PagerDuty: auth-service surge alert fired (rate of failed token_exchanges > 5x baseline)
2026-03-10T06:57Z - Legacy token rotation job (job id job-legacy-rot-93) executed; rotation script hit token-store API concurrently across 150 keys
2026-03-10T07:02Z - Multiple user lockout alerts observed (SRE oncall notified)
2026-03-10T07:20Z - First triage call (Security + IAM + SRE) - preliminary mitigation: paused rotation job
2026-03-10T08:00Z - Investigation: detected unusual external consent attempts for AD app id 0a1b2c3d; flagged for admin review
2026-03-11T09:15Z - Rotated affected service tokens, forced token revocation for orphaned tokens, disabled legacy app consent endpoints
2026-03-12T11:40Z - Post-mitigation monitoring shows auth failure rate back to baseline; continued investigation into phishing correlation
evidence: Auth logs: auth-prod-us-east:/var/log/auth/token_exchange.log lines 2450-2599 show repeated grant_type=refresh_token attempts from client_id legacy-ci-runner
Audit trail: azure-ad-audit-2026-03-10.json contains consent grant requests to app 0a1b2c3d from external-email@example.com (see events 1024-1029)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Recreate the legacy rotation job targeting token-store with a set of orphaned refresh tokens (internal dev-only data).
2) Trigger concurrent refresh attempts to token-exchange endpoint using those tokens and observe lockout rate increase on correlated user principals.
3) Validate that disabling the rotation job stops the amplification.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: rotation job lacked a guard to filter out tokens tagged 'decommissioned' - resource cleanup gap confirmed.
Forensics: two refresh tokens show origin IPs that map to an external CI runner provider; those tokens predate recorded decommissioning by three months.

Phishing correlation: customer's SOC & internal phishing-triage team flagged a suspected phishing email delivered 2026-02-28 to a small engineering group; we are still validating if credentials/tokens were exposed then.
SRE note: token-store API returned 200 for rotation attempts but included 'orphaned' tokens in response set; rotation script did blind replacements rather than atomic transactions.
IAM note: legacy AD app 'legacy-ci-runner' had delegated permissions that permitted refresh flow without interactive consent - risk flagged for removal.
mitigation: Paused legacy token rotation job job-legacy-rot-93 (2026-03-10T07:20Z)
Forced revocation of identified orphaned refresh tokens (2026-03-11T09:15Z)
Disabled external consent endpoint for AD app id 0a1b2c3d and blocked new consents pending review
Invalidated cached session cookies for affected principals and triggered mandatory re-auth for interactive users
Applied temporary IAM rule to reject refresh token requests from the legacy client_id across prod regions
open_action_items: Complete full token-store audit and remove 'decommissioned' tokens permanently - owner: IAM (due 2026-03-17)
Update rotation job to include explicit tag-based filtering and transactional safety - owner: SRE (due 2026-03-19)
Review phishing simulation logs and correlate suspected exposures; report to Security for possible containment follow-up - owner: SecOps (due 2026-03-15)
Create detection rule to alert on token-rotation job spike patterns (owner: Observability team)
resolution: Partial mitigations applied (rotation job paused, tokens revoked, legacy app consent disabled). No confirmed external data exfiltration at present. Full remediation pending token-store cleanup and rotation job hardening. Will elevate to Sev0 only if evidence of credential compromise tied to phishing is confirmed.
